# Image formats

@difference Picture files: TGA, TIFF and JPEG 2000 are not read, but WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, DDS and several other formats are.

The commands that read a picture file all use the same loader: [LoadImage](LoadImage), [LoadAnimImage](LoadAnimImage), [LoadTexture](LoadTexture), [LoadAnimTexture](LoadAnimTexture), [LoadBrush](LoadBrush), [LoadSprite](LoadSprite), [LoadTerrain](LoadTerrain), [LoadBuffer](LoadBuffer), the textures of loaded meshes and levels, and the icons of the gadgets. The format is recognized from the content of the file, not from its name.

The original read what Windows 98 could load: BMP, PNG, JPEG, JPEG 2000, GIF, TGA and TIFF. Here the formats are:

| Format | Original | Here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BMP, PNG, JPEG, GIF | Yes | Yes |
| TGA | Yes | No |
| TIFF | Yes | No |
| JPEG 2000 | Yes | No |
| WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL | No | Yes |
| DDS | No | Yes (block compressed ones stay compressed on the graphics card, see [LoadTexture](LoadTexture)) |
| ICO, CUR, PCX, PNM (PBM, PGM, PPM), QOI, SVG, XPM, XCF, XV, LBM | No | Yes |

TGA is not read because the format has no marker at the start of the file that identifies it, so the loader can only guess it from the file name, which the runtime does not pass on: a TGA file gives 0 even when it is named `.tga`. TIFF is switched off in the build, and nothing reads JPEG 2000. Convert such files to PNG, WebP or another format from the list before loading them. The code for a few of the extra formats (WebP, AVIF and JPEG XL) is in shared libraries that are shipped with the program, and a program that loads such a file warns once if one of them is missing.

Anything that is not in the table, or is damaged, gives 0 from the command (or a runtime error where the command has no way to report it, such as [LoadTerrain](LoadTerrain)).
